beats.headline: A name a dwarf wants revenge on
beats.text: Entered into the file on the word of a dwarf named Arief, who swings his sword and promises revenge. Architect Houston: leader of the Madness, a Viceroy outworlder. He caught Arief's brother trying to sabotage the Madness fortifications, and the brother was tortured before Juice Box got in and ended his suffering. Crawler Donut asks whether this is the one Juice Box decapitated at the pre-production meeting. It is not. That was one of his surgeons. Nobody has managed to get into Houston's lair beside the throne room, which is called his operating theater.

beats.headline: The quiet one at the table
beats.text: Six in the late Queen Imogen's kitchen for a field ruling: three warlords and their adjutants. Architect Houston sits at the far end of the table, unmoving. He was already in the castle, but not in the ballroom when it happened. His adjutant is a tiny floating bune named Opiee. His mask is white and featureless but for a small red teardrop, and his long white robes move as if the body under them is the wrong shape. When Crawler Carl rises with his fists clenched, Houston turns his head toward him. The neck creaks like a wooden ship.

beats.headline: Not culpable, by two votes
beats.text: Panford lays out the charge: Commander Stockade and Architect Houston used secured messaging to reach someone on the eighteenth floor, identified as Nurse Yugoslav of the Madness. Crawler Carl asks, loudly, whether that is his mom. Opiee calls the evidence circumstantial, quite damning, and not enough, and asks his warlord whether he wishes to confess. The masked warlord says nothing. Baroness Victory rules Houston obviously guilty and smart enough to let Stockade do the dirty work, and votes not culpable. Opiee agrees. The Madness is found not guilty of any wrongdoing.

beats.headline: A promise, then a rifle
beats.text: A direct message in the warlord chat: mention his mother out loud again, and Crawler Carl and his animal companion spend their last thousand hours on the amplification table in his surgical theater. This is a promise, he says. A second one: Carl is in mortal danger at this very moment and does not realise it. Then the Lemig Sortion falls, its assets go to the Madness, and Phase One engages. Houston is on his feet with his robes flung back: a bug-like body, six arms, two of them holding a rifle. He fires at Carl's chest. Carl dives, grabs a bag of cat food, and teleports.

beats.headline: The only creature a king fears
beats.text: Filed on the testimony of King Rust, on his saddle outside the Princess Posse lines. Among the reasons he gives Crawler Carl for why the crawlers cannot win: if the orcs did not annihilate them, that lunatic Architect Houston has been using this season's rules to open up his full arsenal. Then the old king admits it. Houston is the only living creature in this universe he fears.

beats.headline: The Beautiful Place
beats.text: At the warlord council Juice Box turns into a tall, black, armless thing with tentacles, and the room recoils. Architect Houston jumps to his feet and leans on the table, shaking, apparently with excitement. Then he explains it, over Epitome Tagg's objections. The creature has a thousand names: the Hag, the Unwashed, the Stalker, the Last Light. The Viceroys, who seek all understanding of life and death, call it the Beautiful Place. Some think it is what people see at the moment of death. Gaining access to it, he adds, is his life's work. Before the meeting is over he is on his feet, pacing.

beats.headline: Joined to a changeling
beats.text: His robes are gone, and so is his mask. Architect Houston is on his back on his own surgical table, and above him the arms of his machine, the Grease Monkey, hold the peeled-open corpse of a changeling named Namico. The machine is connecting the two of them. The System's note on it adds that Houston is prime of the Viceroys because he has made the most discoveries, most of them with this machine. Burcu lies bound on the next table, alive. Eight chained traps ring the room, and his death sets them off. Stay back, he tells Crawler Carl. This is my life's work. I'm almost there.

beats.headline: Died on his own table
beats.text: For the record. Crawler Carl crosses the theater by jumping from table to table. Houston begs him not to press the switch: the changelings are the key to the Beautiful Place, and it was right under their mandibles all along. Carl puts Burcu to sleep and frees her. As Houston's health drains, he sobs that he has found it, that it is really it. Carl throws a healing potion at his head, and he screams at what that has done. Burcu's table tips. Carl's bare feet touch the floor. You don't know what you've done, Houston says, and the traps fire. Credit for the kill: Warlord Carl.
